concept.name: Option chain
concept.definition: An option chain is a quotation display listing all available option series for a given underlying — typically every strike and expiration for both calls and puts — together with bids, asks, last prices, volume, open interest, and often implied volatility and Greeks.
concept.intuition: The option chain is the menu of every option available on a stock or index, laid out so you can compare strikes and expirations at a glance.
concept.mechanics: Chains are organized by expiration date and strike, with calls and puts shown side by side. Traders read chains to select strikes for strategies, gauge liquidity via volume/open interest and bid-ask width, and compute implied volatilities across the surface.
concept.failure_modes: Displayed quotes can be stale or wide on illiquid series, and last-trade prices may be hours old; using last price instead of current bid/ask misstates fair value and strategy P&L.
concept.misconceptions: High volume on a chain line is not proof of 'smart money' direction — it cannot distinguish opening from closing or buying from selling without trade-level data.
concept.example: Pulling up the SPY option chain for the monthly expiry shows strikes from 400 to 600 in $5 steps, with the at-the-money calls quoted at $3.10 bid / $3.20 ask and open interest of 85,000 contracts.
